land.text: the Duchy of Coburg, Ernest III's land, with Königsberg and Sonnefeld (from Saxe-Hildburghausen) and Callenberg and Gauerstadt (from Saxe-Meiningen); Saalfeld went to Meiningen

predecessors.note: The Treaty of Hildburghausen of 12 November 1826, the King of Saxony arbitrating; the new duchy 'was born as a personal union' of Coburg and Gotha under Ernest III as Duke Ernest I.

land.text: Saxe-Gotha, the Gotha half of the extinct Gotha-Altenburg line (1,415 km2 in the 1914 table)

predecessors.note: The Altenburg half became Saxe-Altenburg (saxe-altenburg dossier).

land.text: the state as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918 (the Free State of Coburg and the Free State of Saxe-Gotha)

successors.note: The state was a federal state of the German Empire from 1871 and ended in November 1918 (see the dissolve event); the Weimar Republic took over its land (the Free State of Coburg and the Free State of Saxe-Gotha). The German Empire was its overlord, not its successor, so it is no longer listed here (fx-53 D01, was the 1871 dissolve into german-empire; same change as fx-46 R122 for Bavaria); the hierarchy.csv row saxe-coburg-and-gotha -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator.

ledger.note: 1826: the Treaty of Hildburghausen creates the Duchy of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha. 'King Frederick Augustus of Saxony arbitrated, producing the Treaty of Hildburghausen on 12 November 1826. Ernest III became Duke Ernest I, initially in a personal union with only one Bundesrat vote.' The page names the two duchies and the court's two capitals; the radii are mine.

region.text: Saxe-Gotha, the Gotha lands of the Ernestine division

ledger.note: 1826: Gotha joins Coburg under Ernest I. The new duchy arose from 'the Gothaische Teilung (Gotha division) of the Ernestine duchies' and its 1914 table lists 'Saxe-Gotha 1,415 km2'; the page does not say in so many words that the Gotha lands came from the extinct Gotha-Altenburg line.

region.text: the Districts of Königsberg and Sonnefeld

ledger.note: 1826: Königsberg and Sonnefeld pass from Saxe-Hildburghausen to Coburg. 'Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld received ... the Königsberg and Sonnefeld districts from Saxe-Hildburghausen' (the Saxe-Hildburghausen page: 'Königsberg and Sonnefeld went to the new Duchy of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha'). [Reviewer eu-20-l, 2026-10-31: region set to the two districts the page names (discs as in the duchy-of-saxe-hildburghausen dossier); Königsberg lies about 35 km west of Coburg, outside the Coburg disc]
1826: Callenberg and Gauerstadt pass from Saxe-Meiningen to Coburg. 'Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld received ... Callenberg and Gauerstadt from Saxe-Meiningen.'

region.text: the Principality of Lichtenberg on the Nahe

ledger.note: 1826: the Lichtenberg exclave stays with the new duke. 'Ernest III received the Principality of Lichtenberg from the Congress of Vienna in 1816'; the principality is a dependency ruled from Coburg, drawn as a vassal tint. The year is the new duchy's; the page does not date the dependency to 1826.
1834: Ernest sells Lichtenberg to Prussia. 'He sold it to Prussia in 1834' (the Lichtenberg dossier gives 15 August 1834).

region.text: the state's outline as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918

ledger.note: November 1918 (infobox date 18 November): 'In November 1918, Charles Edward, Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, was forced to abdicate'; infobox 'German Revolution: 18 November 1918'; 'the duchy became two independent states, the Free State of Coburg and the Free State of Saxe-Gotha.' Infobox status 'Federal State of the German Empire (1867-1918)', text 'the German Empire in 1871'. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

certainty.note: Two separate lands (Coburg in the south, Gotha in the north), 70 km apart, given by district names on the pages opened; no boundary survey is described. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes:
Written for batch eu-20-l (2 pages; budget 1-2). The Cliopatria row 'Saxe-Coburg and Gotha' has one shape, 1836-1839 (2,942 km2).

WRONG SHAPE. Nine of its twelve cells lie inside Cliopatria's Saxe-Meiningen 1828 shape (the Hildburghausen and Saalfeld lands that the pages give to Meiningen in 1826); the shape holds Coburg and Sonneberg but no Gotha cell (Gotha sits in the Cliopatria Saxe-Altenburg row, which the saxe-altenburg dossier flags as itself mislabelled). The dossier therefore describes the duchy of 1826 from the pages (Coburg plus Gotha, 1,977 km2 in 1914) with two new keyframes (1826-1835, 1840-1870) and a verdict 'wrong' on 1836-1839, with the same corrected region.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The radii for Coburg (16 km round Coburg) and Gotha (21 km round 10.70E 50.95N) are mine; the pages give district names and the 1914 areas. (2) The page does not say from whom Gotha came (entered as duchy-of-saxe-gotha-altenburg at confidence 2). (3) The Lichtenberg vassal pair is my reading: the page gives only the Congress of Vienna award (1816) and the 1834 sale. (4) End year 1871 follows the sibling dossiers; the monarchy ended in November 1918, Gotha joined Thuringia on 1 May 1920 and Coburg joined Bavaria on 1 July 1920 (page). (5) The Zollverein (1834) and the North German Confederation (1866) are not territorial. No war page was opened: the page does not mention the Austro-Prussian War, so 'wars' is empty.

GAZETTEER NAMES WANTED: Gotha (10.70E 50.95N). The Coburg radius resolves.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIER: duchy-of-saxe-hildburghausen (see the saxe-meiningen dossier).

REVIEW eu-20-l (2026-10-31): removed the 1826 'loss' of Saalfeld to saxe-meiningen (it was never this duchy's land; the page: the Meiningen line 'got from Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld the Saalfelder territories', and duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld already carries that loss); the Königsberg gain region set to the Königsberg and Sonnefeld discs and the Königsberg exclave added to the found, dissolve and keyframe regions. REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (saxe-coburg-and-gotha_1840) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row saxe-coburg-and-gotha -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. After the abdication the duchy became two states, the Free State of Coburg and the Free State of Saxe-Gotha; neither has a dossier, and the dossier keeps one outline to the end.
